en.title: Subarrays with at Least K Disjoint Duplicate Pairs
en.description:
Given an integer array numbers and a positive integer k, count the contiguous subarrays that contain at least k pairs of equal-valued elements. Each pair uses two indices, and indices of different pairs must be pairwise distinct; an element cannot belong to two pairs at once.

The parts marked 'added by this site' and the standard input/output protocol were explicitly compiled by this site; they do not mean the original problem has other unstated rules.
en.input: The first line contains n k; the second line contains n integers. Ranges added by this site: 1≤n≤200000, 1≤k≤10^9, |numbers[i]|≤10^9. When k exceeds the number of pairs the array can provide, the answer is 0.
en.output: Output the number of contiguous subarrays that satisfy the condition.
en.explanation: See the accompanying editorial for the approach, proof of correctness, and complexity.
